candidates.original_title: Memory processes and the course of anxiety and depression in cancer patients
candidates.description: Intrusion and avoidance of intrusive memories do not predict depression at 6-month follow-up after controlling for baseline depression
candidates.citation_sentence: These results partially replicated Brewin et al.'s (1999) finding that both intrusion and avoidance predicted later depression, yet are inconsistent with [6]'s finding that intrusion and avoidance were not predictive.
candidates.notes: [ling26: no entry matched this anchor] Total sample null result is consistent with the original null finding, but the untreated sub-sample showed intrusion significantly predicting depression, which is inconsistent with the original.

candidates.original_title: Memory processes and the course of anxiety and depression in cancer patients
candidates.description: Intrusion and avoidance of intrusive memories predict anxiety at 6-month follow-up
candidates.citation_sentence: Again these findings differed from those of [6] who found that intrusion and avoidance predicted follow-up anxiety, even after controlling for baseline anxiety and stage of cancer illness.
candidates.notes: Neither intrusion nor avoidance predicted anxiety at follow-up in the total sample or the untreated sub-sample, directly contradicting the original finding.

candidates.original_title: Autobiographical memory processes and the course of depression
candidates.description: Intrusion and avoidance of intrusive memories predict depression at 6-month follow-up
candidates.citation_sentence: These results partially replicated Brewin et al.'s (1999) finding that both intrusion and avoidance predicted later depression, yet are inconsistent with [6]'s finding that intrusion and avoidance were not predictive.
candidates.notes: Mixed results: intrusion predicted depression in the untreated sub-sample but not the total sample; avoidance predicted lower depression in the total sample (opposite direction) but not in the untreated sub-sample.

candidates.original_title: Memory processes and the course of anxiety and depression in cancer patients
candidates.description: Intrusion and avoidance of intrusive memories predict depression and anxiety symptoms six months later, controlling for baseline symptoms.
candidates.citation_sentence: These results partially replicated Brewin et al.'s (1999) finding that both intrusion and avoidance predicted later depression, yet are inconsistent with [6]'s finding that intrusion and avoidance were not predictive.
candidates.notes: The paper reports no predictive effect of intrusion or avoidance on follow-up anxiety, contrary to the original anxiety finding, while intrusion predicted depression in untreated participants. The citation to this original appears as reference [6] rather than with author and year in the supplied text.

candidates.original_title: Autobiographical memory processes and the course of depression
candidates.description: Intrusion and avoidance of intrusive memories of stressful life events predict depression symptoms six months later, controlling for baseline depression.
candidates.citation_sentence: These results partially replicated Brewin et al.'s (1999) finding that both intrusion and avoidance predicted later depression, yet are inconsistent with [6]'s finding that intrusion and avoidance were not predictive.
candidates.notes: The authors explicitly describe the result as a partial replication: intrusion predicted later depression among untreated participants, whereas avoidance did not.
